title: US on right AI track; robots take jobs, right tax system needed: Larry Ellison
content: Larry Ellison emphasizes that AI advancements could lead to increased productivity and economic growth. He suggests that taxing the value generated by robots could replace traditional labor taxation methods. This approach could support a universal high income, improving living standards for individuals. Ellison believes that while some jobs may be displaced, automation will create opportunities for more efficient work.

title: Louisiana family's bid to overturn 30-year-old inheritance ruling fails
content: A Louisiana man died without a will in 1956, and a court recognised his daughter as the heir to his estate in 1996. Nearly 30 years later, another family challenged her right to inherit a 50% share of a property. On October 30, the Louisiana Supreme Court rejected the challenge as legally time-barred, upholding the earlier inheritance ruling.

title: Sheep grazing under solar panels boosts honey bees by 83%: Cornell study
content: A recent study from Cornell University demonstrates that allowing sheep to graze beneath solar panels can enhance insect diversity. It found that maintaining two sheep per hectare led to a remarkable 38% rise in beneficial insects, particularly honey bees. As sheep density increased, researchers discovered a critical balance between effective vegetation management and preserving bee health.

title: Woman wins nearly $450,000 after $32,500 flood barrier fails to save home
content: After suffering extensive structural damage to her home from a failing wooden bulkhead, Elizabeth Molbert took legal action against the contractor involved and succeeded. The jury assigned 75% of the blame to the contractor and, in a twist, the appeals court ruled that Molbert had no fault in the matter, increasing her compensation to $448,431.34 and adjusting her mental anguish damages to align with her financial difficulties.

title: Alex Karp buys 37,000 acres of Swedish forest for $22M; why hunters are barred
content: Alex Karp acquired 15,000 hectares of forest land in Härjedalen, Sweden, through his company Cladonia Skog AB. The purchase was confirmed by Svenska Cellulosa Aktiebolaget, which previously owned the forest land. Hunters in the area received notification about the termination of their leasing agreements after the sale. A representative from Cladonia expressed commitment to preserving the natural landscape and its habitats.

title: Georgia city's entire full-time police force quits after mayor tracks chief
content: A small Georgia city is facing a police staffing crisis after its entire full-time police force resigned. Mayor Craig Timmons admitted placing a GPS tracker on Police Chief Lamar Bunn's truck over concerns about his timesheets. Bunn has denied wrongdoing, while the mass resignations have left the city relying on the county sheriff's office for police coverage.

title: Patrick Mahomes opens up about fatherhood and raising three children with Brittany
content: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ popular quarterback, opens p about being there for his children.

title: Andre Agassi and Steffi Graf’s parenting choice kept their children away from tennis spotlight
content: Tennis legends Steffi Graf and Andre Agassi have two children, Jaden and Jaz, but neither followed their parents into professional tennis. Jaden pursued baseball, playing for USC and later representing Team Germany in World Baseball Classic Qualifiers. Jaz developed interests in dancing and horseback riding. The couple deliberately avoided putting sporting pressure on their children, choosing instead to let them discover their own passions and identities.

title: At 1,000 this fiscal, IndiGo set to hire most pilots in a year by an Indian carrier
content: IndiGo has made significant strides by onboarding 600 pilots in just the first half of this fiscal year. With plans to hire an additional 400 by March 2024, the airline is focused on compliance with pilot duty regulations and strategic international expansion. Given the current geopolitical climate, which is influencing operating costs like aviation turbine fuel, IndiGo is evaluating potential fuel hedging strategies to support its long-haul service growth.

title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 polls?
content: Akhilesh Yadav's recent visit to Azam Khan in jail underscores their deep political connection amidst ongoing legal troubles. Following Azam's fleeting bail, the Enforcement Directorate swiftly took him back into custody, adding complexity to the Samajwadi Party's election preparations. Balancing support for Azam while appealing to Muslim constituents presents a significant challenge for Akhilesh as he navigates potential electoral repercussions.

title: Visakhapatnam refinery hit by major fire near oil tank
content: A fire broke out on Monday evening at Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd's Visakh Refinery, causing significant concern in nearby industrial areas. Flames erupted near a tank containing Ruf Pitch Oil, alarming commuters passing by the location and leading to viral videos on social media. HPCL sources reported no injuries or casualties from the incident, but the cause remains unclear. Rumors of an explosion circulated, though officials considered that scenario unlikely.

title: 'Cannot behave like an Indian': HC raps Imran Khan; asks govt to be 'magnanimous'
content: Imran Khan, a US citizen and OCI card holder, faced a Leave India Notice from the Centre. The Bombay high court granted him interim relief after he submitted an unconditional apology. The court clarified that OCI holders don't have the same rights as Indian citizens, particularly regarding protests. Additional Solicitor General Anil Singh argued that the Centre has the power to expel foreigners.

title: Andhra school chainsaw attack: Accused may lose right leg after police encounter
content: Hemanth is facing possible amputation of his right leg due to severe gunshot injuries sustained during a police encounter. He was involved in a chainsaw attack on two minor students at a school in Raptadu. After fleeing, he was located by police who shot at him during a confrontation. One injured student has undergone complex surgeries and is recovering in a hospital in Bengaluru.

title: Historic! 16-yr-old Dhinidhi becomes first Indian swimmer to win a Youth Oly medal
content: India's Dhinidhi Desinghu created history by winning bronze in the women's 100m freestyle at the 2026 Youth Olympics in Dakar, becoming the first Indian female swimmer to medal at the event. The 16-year-old clocked 56.27 seconds. Her coach Nihar Ameen backed her chances of another medal in the 200m freestyle. India also celebrated Khushbu Darjada's judo victory.

title: Pressured for same-sex marriage, 15-year-old school girl dies by suicide
content: A 15-year-old Class 10 student died by suicide at her home on Rahon Road on October 31. Her family has alleged that a 25-year-old woman pressured her for a same-sex marriage through Instagram. The girl's father reported that this pressure caused severe mental stress for his daughter. Police have registered a case against the accused, who has been arrested as part of the ongoing investigation.

title: 'NCP united under Sunetra': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet
content: The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of Ajit Pawar. NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".

title: 9 wickets before IND A call-up! Harsh Dubey scripts history with stunning Ranji spell
content: In a stunning display of skill, Harsh Dubey grabbed nine wickets in a Ranji Trophy clash against Madhya Pradesh, setting a new record for Vidarbha. This remarkable achievement came before he got a spot on India's 15-member squad for the ACC Men's Rising Stars Asia Cup. Having already made his One Day International debut this year, Dubey firmly establishes himself as a promising all-rounder in Indian cricket.

title: Injecting to crush kilos: The rise of ‘Mounjaro’ brides
content: Increasingly, couples in India turn to prescription weight-loss medicines to enhance their appearance before weddings. Clinics in cities like Lucknow report a significant rise in inquiries about these medications. Many individuals seek rapid results to boost confidence for their special day, despite potential health risks. Medical professionals highlight the importance of eligibility criteria and caution against misuse of these drugs.

title: Cuba's hospitals on the brink as US sanctions and oil crisis cripple healthcare
content: Cuba's healthcare landscape is facing serious challenges, as critical medical supplies and equipment run dangerously low. Virtually paralyzed, doctors find it increasingly difficult to deliver effective patient care, with vulnerable groups like malnourished infants and life support-dependent patients at great risk during power outages. The Cuban government recognizes its involvement in this crisis, mainly attributing external issues to US sanctions.

title: Delhi's vehicle ban faces its biggest test at borders: Can enforcement keep up?
content: Delhi is set to implement restrictions on older vehicles that fail to meet BS6 emission standards from entering the city. However, officials are grappling with the difficulty of monitoring numerous entry points, especially during rush hours. Leveraging technology, such as automatic number plate recognition, will be essential for identifying non-compliant vehicles. Collaboration between Delhi and neighboring NCR states is vital to prevent alternative routes and ensure effective enforcement.

title: 'Why should I wake up at 5 am?': Sarfaraz Khan opens up on India snubs & motivation
content: Sarfaraz Khan remains motivated to play cricket despite being overlooked for national selection multiple times. He questions his daily efforts while seeking inspiration from his father's dedication to his career. Although he has performed well in domestic matches, the selector's perception limits his opportunities for overseas play. Sarfaraz's focus on fitness has resulted in significant weight loss and improved performance.

title: ‘Air fares up 700%’: ‘Don’t fly’, says SC as it refuses urgent hearing on Diwali fare surge
content:
SC refuses urgent hearing on plea against steep rise in domestic airfares ahead of Diwali

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Monday refused to urgently list a plea against steep rise in domestic air fares during Diwali season and seeking a direction to Centre to frame a mechanism to cap air fares on domestic routes during festival periods. The issue of regulation of air fares is still pending before SC, a bench hearing the plea was informed while seeking the court's intervention. But the court turned down the plea. Advocate Abhinav for the petitioner submitted that fares have gone up 700% amounts to a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. "Don't travel by air," the bench said. Centre had earlier told SC that the rules on air fares under Bharatiya Vayuyan Adhiniyam, 2024, will be published in two weeks.

End of Article
